look_here_first: Locate cream to white SPHERICAL flower HEADS, not the elongated flower SPIKES of Gregg's/Wright's catclaw. Check hooked twig prickles and a whole bipinnate leaf before confirming from fruit.

morphology_keys.habit: Thorny shrub to small tree of calcareous rocky ground.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate bipinnate; regional floristic key generally 2–4 pinna pairs per leaf, about 6–13 leaflet pairs per pinna, cuneate-oblong leaflets with often glaucous undersides.
morphology_keys.flowers: Short-stalked creamy to white globular/subglobular flower heads (<2x as long as broad), many tiny staminate-looking florets with long protruding stamens.
morphology_keys.armature: Recurved catclaw prickles on woody stems, not paired straight nodal stipular spines.
morphology_keys.pods: Flattened sometimes curved leathery pods; check mature shape, not isolated pod alone.
best_field_traits: Cream-white ROUND flower heads, not narrow flower spikes
Bipinnate leaves, cuneate-oblong leaflets often pale below

comparisons.key_distinctions: Round cream-white heads distinguish from the typically elongated creamy spikes of S. greggii/wrightii. Vachellia flowers often yellow spheres and usually has paired straight stipular spines.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays flora local presence supplied in source pool, but 3 exact target-zone counties not verified; no automatic PASS.

diagnostic_image_needs: round head with nearby bipinnate leaf
flower head macro distinguishing from Vachellia
